title: The pigeon post of Paris
text: In September 1870 Paris found {{1}} besieged by Prussian armies, {{2}} cut the city's telegraph lines and surrounded it entirely. The only way {{3}} carry news across the enemy lines was by carrier pigeon, but a bird can lift only a few grams, and the dispatches kept growing. A photographer named René Dagron solved the problem: printed pages were photographed down {{4}} microfilm weighing a fraction of a gram, and each film was so light {{5}} a pigeon could carry twenty of them at once. Parisians, {{6}} paid a small fee to read the microscopic news under magnifying glasses at the post office, nicknamed the tiny sheets 'pigeon post'. {{7}} is estimated that over a million private messages reached the besieged city {{8}} this improbable airmail service.

gaps.explanation: 'Found itself' — the city experienced its own state.

gaps.hint: relative: armies, ___ cut the telegraph lines
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the armies.

gaps.hint: infinitive: the only way ___ carry news
gaps.explanation: 'The way to do something' — the infinitive modifies 'way'.
'Down onto' — the movement ends on the surface: onto.

gaps.hint: conjunction: so light ___ a pigeon could carry
relative: Parisians, ___ paid a small fee
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative about people after the comma.
'It is estimated that…' — the dummy subject of the passive report.

gaps.hint: preposition: reached the city ___ this service
gaps.explanation: Means of transmission takes 'by': by this service.
